Prediction-Powered Mean Estimation (PPI / PPI++ / Active IPW-PPI)

Source: R/ppi_models.R
ppi_mean.Rd

Estimates the population mean \(\theta^* = \mathbb{E}[Y]\) by combining a human-validated sample (truth_col observed) with a larger LLM-coded unlabeled sample (pred_col only). Implements both standard PPI (lambda = 1) and power-tuned PPI++ (lambda = "auto"), and supports Horvitz-Thompson inverse-probability-weighted (IPW) active/stratified validation designs via weights or inclusion_prob (e.g., produced by select_validation_sample()).

Usage

ppi_mean(
  data,
  truth_col = "human_score",
  pred_col = "llm_score",
  unlabeled = NULL,
  lambda = "auto",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  clip_lambda = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  inclusion_prob = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame (or llm_coded_data) containing truth_col and pred_col. When unlabeled = NULL, rows with non-missing truth_col form the labeled validation set and rows with is.na(truth_col) form the unlabeled set.

truth_col

Name of the numeric human gold-standard column.

pred_col

Name of the numeric LLM prediction column.

unlabeled

Optional separate data.frame of unlabeled observations containing pred_col.

lambda

Power-tuning parameter: "auto" (default, optimal PPI++), 1 (standard PPI), 0 (human-only), or any finite numeric scalar.

conf_level

Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.

clip_lambda

Logical; if TRUE, constrains auto-tuned lambda to [0, 1]. Default FALSE (unconstrained optimal regression control variate is always convex for mean estimation).

weights

Optional Horvitz-Thompson sampling weights \(w_i > 0\) for stratified/active validation sampling: either a column name in data or a numeric vector aligned with data (or the labeled subset). Mutually exclusive with inclusion_prob.

inclusion_prob

Optional validation inclusion probabilities \(\pi_i \in (0, 1]\) (converting to \(w_i = 1 / \pi_i\)): either a column name in data or a numeric vector. Mutually exclusive with weights.

Value

An S3 object of class c("llm_ppi_mean", "llm_ppi") containing $estimates, $benchmarks, $efficiency, $lambda, $vcov, and S3 methods (print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), autoplot()).

Examples

set.seed(42)
n_tot <- 600
y_true <- rnorm(n_tot, mean = 3.5, sd = 1.2)
y_llm <- 0.8 + 0.75 * y_true + rnorm(n_tot, sd = 0.6)
df <- tibble::tibble(
  human_score = c(y_true[1:100], rep(NA_real_, n_tot - 100)),
  llm_score = y_llm
)
fit <- ppi_mean(df, truth_col = "human_score", pred_col = "llm_score")
fit
#> 
#> ── Prediction-Powered Inference (ppi++) 
#> Labeled n = 100 | Unlabeled N = 500 | lambda = 0.814 | CI = 95%
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term   estimate std_error conf_low conf_high p_value var_gain
#>   <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 (Mean)     3.52    0.0789     3.37      3.67 <0.0001     2.51
